name: Built in AI model download and local data
plain: The browser downloads a Gemini Nano model and keeps prompts on the device.
meaning: The model needs about 22 GB free space and a capable GPU or CPU; availability states hint at hardware class.

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: The browser downloads a Gemini Nano model and keeps prompts on the device.

story.what_it_is: Chrome downloads a small AI model to your computer, and prompts stay on your device.

marketing.name: Built-in AI
marketing.pitch: Chrome ships AI models in the browser so sites can add AI features that run on your device with no server calls.

story.for_you: You may see Chrome download a large model in the background, using several gigabytes of space. After that, some AI features run on your device without sending text out. It needs a capable computer.
story.for_makers: Makers get free AI that works offline and keeps user text private. It saves server cost. They must handle devices that cannot run it, and wait for the download.

use_cases.example: A web writing app offers a summary button that runs on your computer, so your private notes do not leave it.
A web chat app checks language and suggests replies on device, so it sends nothing to a server.
A browser game uses the local model for talkative characters, with no cloud cost per player.
A learning site gives writing feedback offline on a school laptop.
A store summarizes long reviews on device, which saves money on AI calls.
A site checks for the model first, and falls back to server AI on devices that do not have it.
A page simplifies hard text on device for a reader who needs plain language.

technical_bounds: Windows 10 or 11, macOS 13+, Linux, ChromeOS Plus
